report:
# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
Originally, obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III of the EU AI Act were set to apply from 2 August 2026 (high confidence). Following the adoption of the "AI Omnibus" simplification package (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744), this date was postponed to 2 December 2027, with a further extension to 2 August 2028 for high-risk systems embedded in products covered by existing Union harmonisation legislation (high confidence). A low-confidence, uncorroborated source claims an even later 2029 deadline, but this is not supported by official EU channels.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (Pre-Omnibus)
Under the originally adopted AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), Chapter III Sections 1-3—covering the high-risk obligations tied to Annex III—were scheduled to apply from 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [EU AI Act Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)). Several news and compliance-advisory sources continued to describe 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline without acknowledging the later Omnibus amendment, a claim rated low confidence (0.17) given its reliance on outdated, lower-authority sources ([Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20), [Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance)).

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
The AI Omnibus / Digital Package on Simplification was adopted on 19 November 2025, reached political agreement on 7 May 2026, and entered into force on 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai), [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). The European Commission proposed adjusting the high-risk rules' timeline by up to 16 months so that obligations would take effect once the Commission confirms that necessary standards and compliance tools are available (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

### Current Applicable Dates
As amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, the obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence), as confirmed across multiple official EU sources ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force), [AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)). High-risk AI systems that are safety components of products, or are themselves products, covered by Union harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I have an extended application date of **2 August 2028** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act), [European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)).

### Grandfathering and Related Provisions
Article 113 and Article 111(2) provide that the Regulation applies to operators of certain high-risk AI systems already placed on the market or put into service before the Chapter III application date only if those systems undergo significant design changes from that date onward (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)). Separately, transparency obligations under Article 50 generally apply from 2 August 2026, with a transition until 2 December 2026 for legacy systems—these are distinct from the Annex III high-risk deadlines and should not be conflated (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Most official EU sources and legal analyses converge on 2 December 2027 as the Omnibus-amended Annex III deadline, but one uncorroborated source claims a further delay to **2 August 2029**, citing an unverified "September 2026" agreement (low confidence, 0.12) ([unverified blog](https://ai-act-news-blog.example/annex-iii-deadline-update)). No official EU source supports this 2029 date, and it should be treated with significant skepticism.

Several lower-authority sources still cite 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline, rated low confidence (0.17), reflecting either outdated pre-Omnibus information or failure to track regulatory amendments ([Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20), [McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026)).

A separate claim describing a generic "36 months after entry into force" rule (~August 2027) does not match the Omnibus-specific 2 December 2027 date, suggesting it predates the amendment (medium confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence)).

## Knowledge Gaps
- Whether Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 is the final, legally confirmed instrument, or whether further delays (e.g., to 2029) are under consideration remains unclear given the single uncorroborated source.
- The interaction between the Article 111(2)/113 grandfathering rule and the new 2 December 2027 date (versus the old 2026 date) is not fully specified in available sources.
- It is unclear whether all eight Annex III use-case categories share the same 2 December 2027 date or whether sub-category exceptions exist.
- Consequences of continued unavailability of harmonised standards or notified-body capacity by the 2027 deadline are not addressed.

This report was produced by an automated research pipeline: web search, source classification, confidence scores computed from source authority, recency and corroboration, and an automated review against the extracted claims.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
Originally, obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III of the EU AI Act were set to apply from 2 August 2026 (high confidence). Following the adoption of the "AI Omnibus" simplification package (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744), this date was postponed to 2 December 2027, with a further extension to 2 August 2028 for high-risk systems embedded in products covered by existing Union harmonisation legislation (high confidence). A low-confidence, uncorroborated source claims an even later 2029 deadline, but this is not supported by official EU channels.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (Pre-Omnibus)
Under the originally adopted AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), Chapter III Sections 1-3—covering the high-risk obligations tied to Annex III—were scheduled to apply from 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [EU AI Act Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)). Several news and compliance-advisory sources continued to describe 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline without acknowledging the later Omnibus amendment (medium-low confidence) ([Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20), [Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance)).

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
The AI Omnibus / Digital Package on Simplification was adopted on 19 November 2025, reached political agreement on 7 May 2026, and entered into force on 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai), [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). The European Commission proposed adjusting the high-risk rules' timeline by up to 16 months so that obligations would take effect once the Commission confirms that necessary standards and compliance tools are available (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

### Current Applicable Dates
As amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, the obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence), as confirmed across multiple official EU sources ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force), [AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)). High-risk AI systems that are safety components of products, or are themselves products, covered by Union harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I have an extended application date of **2 August 2028** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act), [European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)).

### Grandfathering and Related Provisions
Article 113 and Article 111(2) provide that the Regulation applies to operators of certain high-risk AI systems already placed on the market or put into service before the Chapter III application date only if those systems undergo significant design changes from that date onward (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)). Separately, transparency obligations under Article 50 generally apply from 2 August 2026, with a transition until 2 December 2026 for legacy systems—these are distinct from the Annex III high-risk deadlines and should not be conflated (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Most official EU sources and legal analyses converge on 2 December 2027 as the Omnibus-amended Annex III deadline, but one uncorroborated source claims a further delay to **2 August 2029**, citing an unverified "September 2026" agreement (low confidence, flagged: confidence 0.12) ([unverified blog](https://ai-act-news-blog.example/annex-iii-deadline-update)). No official EU source supports this 2029 date, and it should be treated with significant skepticism.

Several lower-authority sources still cite 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline (low-medium confidence, flagged: confidence 0.17), reflecting either outdated pre-Omnibus information or failure to track regulatory amendments ([Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20), [McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026)).

A separate claim describing a generic "36 months after entry into force" rule (~August 2027) does not match the Omnibus-specific 2 December 2027 date, suggesting it predates the amendment (medium confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence)).

## Knowledge Gaps
- Whether Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 is the final, legally confirmed instrument, or whether further delays (e.g., to 2029) are under consideration remains unclear given the single uncorroborated source.
- The interaction between the Article 111(2)/113 grandfathering rule and the new 2 December 2027 date (versus the old 2026 date) is not fully specified in available sources.
- It is unclear whether all eight Annex III use-case categories share the same 2 December 2027 date or whether sub-category exceptions exist.
- Consequences of continued unavailability of harmonised standards or notified-body capacity by the 2027 deadline are not addressed.
